import unittest

    Parses a CSV string into a list of lists.
    Supports quoted fields and escaped double quotes ("" inside quotes).

    reader = csv.reader(io.StringIO(csv_string))
    return [row for row in reader]

rows.text:
A database index is fundamentally a data structure that improves the speed of data retrieval operations on a database table at the cost of additional writes and storage space. To understand how it works, one must first grasp the inefficiency of a full table scan. Without an index, if you ask a database to find a specific record, it must read every single row in the table from start to finish until it finds a match. This is analogous to looking for a specific word in a dictionary by reading every page from the beginning. An index acts like the alphabetical index at the back of that dictionary, allowing you to jump directly to the relevant page.

The most common type of index is the B-Tree (Balanced Tree). In a B-Tree, data is organized in a hierarchical structure where each node contains keys and pointers to child nodes. This structure is self-balancing, ensuring that the tree remains shallow even as the amount of data grows. This shallow depth is crucial for performance because it minimizes the number of disk I/O operations required to locate data. Disk access is significantly slower than memory access, so reducing the number of times the database engine needs to touch the physical disk is the primary way indexes speed up queries.

Without an index, if you ask a database to find a specific record, such as a user with the email "john.doe@example.com," the database engine must read every single row in the table from start to finish until it finds a match. This process, known as a linear search, has a time complexity of O(n), meaning the time required grows linearly with the number of rows. For a table with millions of records, this is prohibitively slow. An index solves this by creating a separate, optimized structure that allows the database to jump directly to the relevant data, much like the index at the back of a textbook allows you to find a topic without reading every page.
